title: Lean-Verified Proof of Sendov’s Conjecture for All Degrees n ≥ 2
whyItMatters: Independent researcher Lech Mazur used GPT-5.6 Pro and Lean 4 to close the 67-year-old Sendov conjecture for every polynomial degree n ≥ 2; Terence Tao digested and streamlined the proof.
summary: Sendov’s 1959 conjecture asserts that if all roots of a complex polynomial lie in the unit disk, every root has a critical point within distance 1. Terence Tao had previously resolved sufficiently high degrees (2020) without an explicit threshold; in August 2026, independent researcher Lech Mazur used AI agents through ProofAtlas to obtain a complete, remarkably elementary Lean-verified proof for all n ≥ 2. Tao published an expository digestion and shorter Lean formalization, noting the argument also settles the stronger Phelps–Rodriguez conjecture.
technicalHighlights: Closed the finite-degree gap left by Tao’s 2020 asymptotic theorem with a unified, elementary argument valid for every degree n ≥ 2.
Fully verified in Lean 4 both by ProofAtlas and in Terence Tao’s independent streamlined repository (teorth/sendov).
Simultaneously implied the stronger Phelps–Rodriguez conjecture as noted by Tao.
caveats: Initial AI-assisted manuscript was verbose and certificate-heavy until streamlined in Tao’s digestion and follow-up arXiv exposition (2609.04246).

scoreRationale.foundational: Settled a famous 67-year-old conjecture in complex analysis for all degrees, plus Phelps–Rodriguez.
scoreRationale.ripple: Showed independent researchers outside academia can produce Lean-verified resolutions verified by Fields Medalists.
scoreRationale.verification: Double-verified in Lean 4 (Mazur and teorth/sendov) and digested line-by-line by Terence Tao.
scoreRationale.velocity: Completed a 67-year-old problem via an AI-curated elementary scalar optimization proof in days.
